question: Which of the following tribe was very influential in Punjab during the thirteenth and fourteenth century?
solution_text:
The correct answer is The Khokhar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Khokhars (खोखर) were a powerful and warlike tribe of the Punjab region who were very influential during the thirteenth and fourteenth centuries.

• They frequently rebelled against the rulers of the Delhi Sultanate and were known for their resistance in the north-western frontier region.

• Their leaders like Jasrat Khokhar played an important role in the politics of Punjab in the early fifteenth century as well.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Khokhars were associated with the region around the rivers Jhelum and Chenab.

• They rose in rebellion during the reign of the Ghurids and later the Tughlaqs.

• The tribe finds mention in the accounts of medieval chroniclers dealing with the Punjab frontier.

NOTE

• The Gond (Option 2): A large Dravidian-speaking tribe mainly found in central India (Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra), known for the Gondwana kingdoms.

• The Santhal (Option 3): One of the largest tribes of eastern India (Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha), famous for the Santhal Rebellion (1855-56).

• The Bhil (Option 4): A major tribe of western and central India (Rajasthan, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh), often called the 'bowmen of India'.

question:
Which of the following pairs is correct regarding the campaign years of Akbar at various places?
I. Ranthambore- 1569
II. Gujarat- 1572
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Both the given pairs regarding the military campaigns of Akbar (अकबर के अभियान) are correctly matched.

• Akbar conquered the fort of Ranthambore in 1569 from the Hada Rajputs under Rai Surjan Hada.

• Akbar annexed Gujarat in 1572 (completed by 1573), after which he built the Buland Darwaza at Fatehpur Sikri to commemorate the victory.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Akbar captured Chittorgarh in 1568 after a prolonged siege.

• The conquest of Gujarat gave the Mughals access to profitable sea trade and ports.

• Akbar ruled from 1556 to 1605 and was the third Mughal emperor.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, because statement II (Gujarat- 1572) is also correct, not just statement I.

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, because statement I (Ranthambore- 1569) is also correct, not just statement II.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, because both statements are correctly matched with their campaign years.

question: Who was the First Indian actress to win an international award at the 1963 Moscow International Film Festival?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Suchitra Sen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Suchitra Sen (सुचित्रा सेन) became the first Indian actress to win an international award when she won the Best Actress (Silver Prize) at the 1963 Moscow International Film Festival.

• She won it for her performance in the Bengali film 'Saat Paake Bandha' (1963).

• She was a legendary actress of Bengali and Hindi cinema and was awarded the Padma Shri.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Suchitra Sen was honoured with the Banga Bibhushan by the Government of West Bengal.

• Her famous pairing with actor Uttam Kumar is iconic in Bengali cinema.

• She declined the Dadasaheb Phalke Award as she preferred to stay away from the public eye in her later years.

NOTE

• Nargis Dutt (Option 1): Renowned actress of Hindi cinema (Mother India), the first female recipient of the Padma Shri among actresses and later a Rajya Sabha member.

• Zeenat Aman (Option 3): Popular Hindi film actress of the 1970s-80s, known for films like Hare Rama Hare Krishna and Satyam Shivam Sundaram.

• Jaya Prada (Option 4): South Indian and Hindi film actress and later a politician who served as a Member of Parliament.

question: Who was the first Indian to be awarded the Nobel Prize?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rabindranath Tagore.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rabindranath Tagore (रवींद्रनाथ टैगोर) was the first Indian (and first Asian) to be awarded a Nobel Prize.

• He received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913 for his collection of poems 'Gitanjali'.

• He was a poet, writer, painter and composer who wrote India's national anthem 'Jana Gana Mana' and Bangladesh's 'Amar Sonar Bangla'.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Tagore founded Visva-Bharati University at Santiniketan.

• He renounced his knighthood in protest against the Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 1919.

• He is popularly known as 'Gurudev', 'Kabiguru' and 'Biswakabi'.

NOTE

• Amartya Sen (Option 1): Indian economist who won the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences in 1998 for his work on welfare economics.

• Kailash Satyarthi (Option 2): Indian child-rights activist who shared the Nobel Peace Prize in 2014 with Malala Yousafzai.

• Subramanian Chandrashekar (Option 4): Indian-American astrophysicist who won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1983 (Chandrasekhar limit).

question: Swavalambini that was launched in March 2025 is a ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is women Entrepreneurship Programme.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Swavalambini (स्वावलंबिनी - महिला उद्यमिता कार्यक्रम) is a Women Entrepreneurship Programme launched in March 2025.

• It was launched by Union Minister Shri Jayant Chaudhary and is implemented by NIESBUD and IIE under the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.

• Its aim is to nurture entrepreneurial mindset and skills among women students in higher educational institutions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The programme includes an Entrepreneurship Orientation Programme, an Entrepreneurship Awareness Programme and an Entrepreneurship Development Programme.

• It is aligned with the goal of empowering women and promoting self-reliance (Atmanirbhar).

• NIESBUD stands for the National Institute for Entrepreneurship and Small Business Development.

NOTE

• financial Literacy Campaign (Option 2): A general term for programmes that spread awareness about savings, banking and investment; not what Swavalambini is.

• digital Inclusion Project (Option 3): Refers to initiatives to bridge the digital divide; not the objective of Swavalambini.

• childcare Support Initiative (Option 4): Relates to schemes supporting child care and welfare; unrelated to this women entrepreneurship programme.

question: In 2025, PM SVANidhi was enhanced with UPI-linked credit cards for street vendors. Which Ministry oversees this?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ministry of Housing & Urban Affairs.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• PM SVANidhi (पीएम स्वनिधि योजना) is overseen by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA).

• In 2025, the scheme was enhanced to provide UPI-linked credit cards to street vendors, along with higher collateral-free working capital loans.

• PM SVANidhi (PM Street Vendor's AtmaNirbhar Nidhi) was launched in June 2020 to support urban street vendors.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The scheme provides collateral-free working capital loans in tranches, with interest subsidy for timely repayment.

• It promotes digital transactions among street vendors through cashback incentives.

• The 2025 Union Budget announced an enhanced version of the scheme benefiting lakhs of street vendors.

NOTE

• Ministry of Finance (Option 1): Handles budget, taxation and financial policy, but does not administer PM SVANidhi.

• Ministry of Commerce & Industry (Option 3): Deals with trade, industry and export-import policy, not street vendor welfare.

• Ministry of MSME (Option 4): Looks after micro, small and medium enterprises and schemes like PMEGP, not PM SVANidhi.

question: In World Press Freedom Index 2025, which of the following countries is worst performer?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Eritrea.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the World Press Freedom Index 2025 (वर्ल्ड प्रेस फ्रीडम सूचकांक), Eritrea was the worst performer, ranked last at 180th position.

• The index is released annually by Reporters Without Borders (RSF).

• The 2025 report highlighted economic fragility as a leading threat to press freedom worldwide.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Norway topped the index as the country with the greatest press freedom.

• India was ranked 151st in the World Press Freedom Index 2025.

• More than half of the world's population was reported to live in 'red zones' of press freedom.

NOTE

• Pakistan (Option 2): Ranked low but not the worst; it faces significant press freedom challenges but was placed above Eritrea.

• Sudan (Option 3): A conflict-hit country with poor press freedom, yet it did not occupy the last position.

• Nepal (Option 4): Ranked considerably higher than the bottom countries in the 2025 index.

question: What is the India's cumulative solar power capacity (in GW) as of July 2025?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 119.02.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• India's cumulative solar power capacity (सौर ऊर्जा क्षमता) reached about 119.02 GW as of July 2025.

• Solar power accounted for over 60% of India's total renewable energy installed capacity at that time.

• This growth reflects India's push toward its target of 500 GW of non-fossil fuel capacity by 2030.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• India crossed the milestone of 50% non-fossil fuel installed power capacity in 2025.

• Rajasthan and Gujarat are among the leading states in solar power capacity.

• The National Solar Mission (part of the National Action Plan on Climate Change) drives India's solar targets.

NOTE

• 50 (Option 1): This was roughly India's solar capacity around 2021-22, not July 2025.

• 67.75 (Option 2): An intermediate figure that does not match the July 2025 cumulative capacity.

• 175 (Option 4): 175 GW was India's overall renewable energy target for 2022, not the solar capacity in July 2025.

question: Who is the author of the book 'Speedpost', a collection of personal letters to her children?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shobha De.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shobha De (शोभा डे) is the author of the book 'Speedpost', a collection of personal letters written to her children.

• She is a well-known Indian columnist and novelist, often called the 'Jackie Collins of India'.

• The book offers advice and reflections on life, relationships and parenting in an epistolary form.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Her other notable works include 'Socialite Evenings', 'Starry Nights' and 'Second Thoughts'.

• She began her career as a model and later became a journalist and magazine editor.

• Her writing often focuses on urban Indian society and women.

NOTE

• Kiran Desai (Option 1): Won the Man Booker Prize in 2006 for 'The Inheritance of Loss'.

• Jhumpa Lahiri (Option 3): Won the Pulitzer Prize for her short story collection 'Interpreter of Maladies'.

• Arundhati Roy (Option 4): Won the Booker Prize in 1997 for 'The God of Small Things'.

question: Which of the following period is known as the "Golden age" of Indian temple architecture?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gupta period.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Gupta period (गुप्त काल) is known as the 'Golden Age' of ancient India, including in the field of temple architecture.

• The earliest surviving structural Hindu temples in the true sense were built during this era, such as the Dashavatara Temple at Deogarh.

• The Guptas ruled roughly from the 4th to the 6th century CE.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Gupta-era temples marked the beginning of the Nagara (North Indian) style of temple architecture.

• The Iron Pillar of Delhi and the Ajanta cave paintings also belong to this period.

• Notable Gupta rulers include Chandragupta I, Samudragupta and Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya).

NOTE

• Maurya Period (Option 2): Known for rock-cut architecture, Ashokan pillars and stupas, not temple architecture.

• Delhi Sultanate Period (Option 3): Associated with Indo-Islamic architecture such as the Qutub Minar, not Hindu temple architecture.

• Mughal Period (Option 4): Famous for monuments like the Taj Mahal and Red Fort in Indo-Islamic style, not the golden age of temple building.

question: Which of the following is popular dance of the state of Himachal Pradesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shand and Shabu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Shand and Shabu (शांड और शबू) is a popular folk dance of the state of Himachal Pradesh.

• It is performed in the Lahaul valley, generally in the monastery courtyards, and is associated with Buddhist tradition.

• Himachal Pradesh has a rich tradition of folk dances tied to festivals and religious occasions.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Other folk dances of Himachal Pradesh include Nati, Kayang, Bakayang and Chham.

• Nati of Himachal Pradesh has been recognised as one of the largest folk dances in the Guinness World Records.

• These dances are usually performed to the beat of traditional drums and instruments.

NOTE

• Fugdi (Option 1): A folk dance of Goa and the Konkan region, performed by women during festivals.

• Sattriya (Option 2): A classical dance form of Assam, originating in the Vaishnava monasteries (Sattras).

• Jhumar (Option 3): A folk dance associated with Punjab, Haryana and Rajasthan.

question: Within ______ years from the Big Bang, temperature dropped to 4500K (Kelvin) and gave rise to atomic matter. The universe became transparent.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 300000.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Within about 300000 years from the Big Bang (बिग बैंग), the temperature of the universe dropped to around 4500 K, allowing electrons and nuclei to combine into neutral atoms (atomic matter).

• This event is known as recombination, after which the universe became transparent to radiation.

• The radiation released at this stage is observed today as the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Big Bang theory was proposed by Georges Lemaitre.

• The term 'Big Bang' was coined by Fred Hoyle.

• The CMB was discovered by Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson, supporting the Big Bang theory.

NOTE

• 3000 (Option 2): Too short a time period; neutral atoms had not yet formed at this stage.

• 30000 (Option 3): The universe was still too hot and ionised at this point for atoms to form stably.

• 300 (Option 4): In the first few hundred years the universe was extremely hot and opaque, dominated by a plasma of charged particles.

question: In January 2025, which country has developed the World's Most powerful hydrogen train engine?
solution_text:
The correct answer is India.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In January 2025, India (भारत) developed the world's most powerful hydrogen train engine.

• The engine has a capacity of about 1200 HP, higher than the hydrogen train engines developed by other countries.

• It was developed by Indian Railways as part of the 'Hydrogen for Heritage' initiative.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The first hydrogen train trial in India is planned on the Jind-Sonipat route in Haryana.

• Hydrogen trains are zero-emission as they emit only water vapour.

• The Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw announced this achievement.

NOTE

• Germany (Option 2): Operated the world's first hydrogen-powered passenger trains (Coradia iLint by Alstom), but with lower-power engines.

• Japan (Option 3): Has been testing hydrogen-powered trains (Hybari), but did not develop the most powerful engine.

• France (Option 4): Home to Alstom, a maker of hydrogen trains, but not the developer of the most powerful engine in this context.

question: The object covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time, it is said to be in ______ motion.
solution_text:
The correct answer is non-uniform.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When an object covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time, it is said to be in non-uniform motion (नॉन-यूनिफार्म / असमान गति).

• In non-uniform motion, the speed of the object keeps changing, so the object has acceleration.

• Example: a car moving through heavy traffic with changing speed.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• In uniform motion, the object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time.

• Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity with respect to time.

• A distance-time graph of non-uniform motion is a curved line, while that of uniform motion is a straight line.

NOTE

• uniform (Option 1): Motion in which an object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time; the opposite of what is described.

• linear (Option 2): Refers to motion along a straight line; it describes the path, not the equal/unequal distance property.

• circular (Option 4): Motion of an object along a circular path; not defined by covering unequal distances in equal times.

question: Which of the following battles was fought in 1761?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Third Battle of Panipat.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Third Battle of Panipat (पानीपत की तीसरी लड़ाई) was fought in 1761.

• It was fought between the Marathas and the Afghan forces of Ahmad Shah Abdali (Durrani).

• The Marathas were defeated, which checked their expansion in northern India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Maratha forces were led by Sadashiv Rao Bhau.

• Panipat, located in present-day Haryana, was the site of three historic battles (1526, 1556, 1761).

• The battle resulted in heavy loss of life for the Marathas.

NOTE

• First Battle of Panipat (Option 2): Fought in 1526 between Babur and Ibrahim Lodi, marking the start of Mughal rule in India.

• Second Battle of Tarain (Option 3): Fought in 1192 between Muhammad Ghori and Prithviraj Chauhan, won by Ghori.

• First Battle of Tarain (Option 4): Fought in 1191 between Prithviraj Chauhan and Muhammad Ghori, won by Prithviraj Chauhan.

question: In the context of Budget, the salaries, pensions, defence services comes under ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is revenue expenditure.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Salaries, pensions and expenditure on defence services (except asset creation) come under revenue expenditure (राजस्व व्यय).

• Revenue expenditure is the expenditure that neither creates any asset nor reduces any liability of the government.

• It is a recurring expenditure incurred for the normal functioning of the government.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Capital expenditure creates assets or reduces liabilities, e.g., building roads or repaying loans.

• Interest payments and subsidies are also part of revenue expenditure.

• The Budget is divided into Revenue Budget and Capital Budget.

NOTE

• revenue receipts (Option 2): Income of the government that neither creates a liability nor reduces an asset, e.g., taxes; these are receipts, not expenditure.

• capital receipts (Option 3): Receipts that create a liability or reduce an asset, e.g., borrowings and disinvestment proceeds.

• capital expenditure (Option 4): Expenditure that creates assets or reduces liabilities, such as construction of infrastructure or loan repayment.

question: The Deepak Parekh committee to look into various aspects of providing affordable housing was set up in which year?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2008.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Deepak Parekh Committee (दीपक पारेख समिति) to look into various aspects of providing affordable housing was set up in 2008.

• It was constituted as a High Level Task Force on Affordable Housing for All.

• The committee gave recommendations on making housing affordable for the economically weaker sections and low-income groups.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Deepak Parekh is a noted banker associated with HDFC.

• The committee defined affordable housing in terms of income levels, size of dwelling and affordability.

• Its recommendations influenced later housing policies and schemes in India.

NOTE

• 2001 (Option 2): Not the year the committee was set up; it is incorrect.

• 2005 (Option 3): An incorrect year; the affordable housing task force was formed later.

• 2011 (Option 4): Also incorrect; the committee predates this year.

question: The Hirakud Dam project is a multipurpose scheme intended for flood control, irrigation and power generation. It is built across ______ river.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahanadi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Hirakud Dam (हीराकुंड बांध) is built across the Mahanadi (महानदी) river in the state of Odisha.

• It is a multipurpose project intended for flood control, irrigation and hydroelectric power generation.

• It is one of the longest earthen dams in the world.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Hirakud Dam was inaugurated in 1957 and is located near Sambalpur in Odisha.

• The Mahanadi river rises in Chhattisgarh and flows into the Bay of Bengal.

• The reservoir formed by the dam is known as the Hirakud Reservoir.

NOTE

• Periyar (Option 1): A river in Kerala; the Mullaperiyar Dam is built on it, not Hirakud.

• Krishna (Option 2): A major peninsular river; dams like Nagarjuna Sagar and Srisailam are built on it.

• Indus (Option 4): A major river of the Indian subcontinent; the Tarbela Dam (in Pakistan) is built on it.

question: Which of the following state is rich in sandstone, granite and marble?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rajasthan (राजस्थान) is rich in building and dimensional stones like sandstone, granite and marble.

• Makrana in Rajasthan is famous for its high-quality white marble, which was used in the Taj Mahal.

• The state is a leading producer of marble and sandstone in India.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Rajasthan is also rich in minerals like zinc, lead, copper and gypsum.

• Jodhpur and Dholpur are known for their red and beige sandstone.

• Kishangarh in Rajasthan is a major marble trading hub.

NOTE

• Kerala (Option 1): Known for resources like monazite, ilmenite and spices, not primarily for granite-marble-sandstone.

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 2): Produces granite and barytes, but it is not the answer emphasised for all three stones together.

• Odisha (Option 3): Rich in minerals like iron ore, bauxite and chromite, rather than marble and sandstone.

question: What was the literacy rate of India as per census 1951?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 18.33%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census of 1951 (1951 की जनगणना), the literacy rate of India was 18.33%.

• This was the first census conducted after India's independence.

• The male literacy rate was higher than the female literacy rate at that time.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• As per Census 2011, the literacy rate of India was 74.04%.

• Kerala has consistently recorded the highest literacy rate among Indian states.

• The Census in India is conducted every ten years; the first was in 1872 and the first complete one in 1881.

NOTE

• 28.33% (Option 2): An incorrect figure; the 1951 literacy rate was much lower.

• 10.33% (Option 3): Closer to pre-independence literacy levels but not the 1951 figure.

• 9.33% (Option 4): Incorrect; this does not represent the 1951 literacy rate.

question:
Which of the following is a sub-field of social geography?
I. Gender Geography
II. Cultural Geography
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both I and II.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Both Gender Geography and Cultural Geography are sub-fields of Social Geography (सामाजिक भूगोल).

• Social geography studies the relationship between society and space, including social groups and their spatial patterns.

• Its sub-fields also include behavioural geography, geography of social well-being, geography of leisure and historical social geography.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Human geography is broadly divided into social, economic, political, historical and population geography.

• Cultural geography studies cultural products and norms and their spatial variation.

• Gender geography examines how gender relations shape and are shaped by space and place.

NOTE

• Only I (Option 1): Incorrect, because Cultural Geography (II) is also a sub-field of social geography.

• Only II (Option 2): Incorrect, because Gender Geography (I) is also a sub-field of social geography.

• Neither I nor II (Option 4): Incorrect, because both are recognised sub-fields of social geography.

question: The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act-2003 mandates the central government to reduce fiscal deficit to not more than ______ of GDP.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act, 2003 (राजकोषीय उत्तरदायित्व और बजट प्रबंधन अधिनियम) mandates the central government to reduce the fiscal deficit to not more than 3% of GDP.

• The Act aims to ensure fiscal discipline and inter-generational equity in fiscal management.

• It also originally targeted the elimination of the revenue deficit.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The FRBM Act was enacted to institutionalise financial discipline and improve macroeconomic management.

• The N.K. Singh Committee reviewed the FRBM framework and recommended a debt-to-GDP target.

• An 'escape clause' allows the government to deviate from targets under specified conditions.

NOTE

• 1% (Option 1): Not the fiscal deficit target under the FRBM Act.

• 2% (Option 2): Incorrect; the FRBM Act sets the fiscal deficit ceiling at 3% of GDP.

• 8% (Option 4): Far above the prescribed limit; incorrect for the fiscal deficit target.

question: What role do cellular vacuoles play in plant waste management?
solution_text:
The correct answer is They store waste products.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In plants, the vacuoles (कोशिकीय रिक्तिकाएं) play an important role in waste management by storing waste products and toxic by-products.

• The large central vacuole in plant cells stores water, ions, nutrients and waste materials.

• Since plants do not have a well-developed excretory system, they store waste in vacuoles and old tissues.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The vacuole is bound by a membrane called the tonoplast.

• Vacuoles also help maintain turgor pressure, keeping the plant cell firm.

• Some waste products are stored as crystals or are removed when leaves and bark are shed.

NOTE

• They facilitate nutrient absorption (Option 1): Nutrient absorption in plants is mainly done by root hairs, not the role emphasised here for vacuoles.

• They assist in photosynthesis (Option 3): Photosynthesis takes place in chloroplasts, not vacuoles.

• They help in water transportation (Option 4): Water transport occurs through the xylem tissue, not the vacuoles.

question: Under the policy of matrimonial alliances, Bimbisara married the sister of which king of Kosala?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prasenjit.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under his policy of matrimonial alliances, Bimbisara (बिंबिसार) married Kosala Devi, the sister of Prasenjit (प्रसेनजीत), the king of Kosala.

• As dowry, Bimbisara received the village of Kashi, which strengthened Magadha.

• Bimbisara was a ruler of the Haryanka dynasty of Magadha and a contemporary of Gautam Buddha and Mahavira.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Bimbisara also married Chellana, a Lichchhavi princess of Vaishali, and a princess from the Madra clan of Punjab.

• His capital was Rajgir (Girivraja).

• He was succeeded by his son Ajatashatru.

NOTE

• Chetak (Option 1): Chetaka was the Lichchhavi chief of Vaishali (also famous as Maharana Pratap's horse), not the king of Kosala.

• Ajatashatru (Option 2): The son and successor of Bimbisara who expanded the Magadha empire.

• Brahmadatta (Option 4): A legendary king of Kashi mentioned in Buddhist Jataka tales, not the Kosala king in this context.

question: Gautamiputra Satakarni, who ruled in the first century AD, is regarded as the greatest among which dynasty's rulers?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Satavahana rulers.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Gautamiputra Satakarni (गौतमीपुत्र शातकर्णी) is regarded as the greatest among the Satavahana (सातवाहन) rulers.

• He ruled in the first-second century AD and revived the fortunes of the Satavahana dynasty.

• He defeated the Western Kshatrapa ruler Nahapana and expanded his kingdom.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Satavahanas ruled over the Deccan region and are also known as the Andhras.

• Details of Gautamiputra Satakarni's achievements are known from the Nashik Prashasti inscription of his mother Gautami Balashri.

• The Satavahanas were the first native Indian rulers to issue coins with the portraits of their rulers.

NOTE

• Gupta rulers (Option 1): Ruled from the 4th-6th century CE; Chandragupta II and Samudragupta were their greatest kings.

• Maurya rulers (Option 2): Ruled from around 322 BCE; Chandragupta Maurya and Ashoka were prominent rulers.

• Chola rulers (Option 3): A South Indian dynasty famous for rulers like Rajaraja I and Rajendra I, who reigned much later.
